boundary_rationale: Zion's own prayer closes the poem: “Look, Yahweh, and see to whom you have done thus!” web:Lam.2.20, opening on the same petition imperative רְאֵ֤ה יְהוָה֙ וְֽהַבִּ֔יטָה (oshb:Lam.2.20, byte tier) that already stood at oshb:Lam.1.11 (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier), then presses that plea through the horror of women eating their own children and priest and prophet slain in the sanctuary before turning to the day of slaughter itself: “You have called, as in the day of a solemn assembly, my terrors on every side.” web:Lam.2.22. The three-token form בְּי֥וֹם אַף יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Lam.2.22, byte tier; roughly "in the day of the anger of Yahweh") stands in exactly 1 verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse book-wide, this three-token form) and so closes the poem as a form attested once, not a repeating pattern; the shorter token it opens with, בְּי֥וֹם (oshb:Lam.2.22, byte tier), is itself byte-identical to the token that opens the same wrath phrase at the poem's own aleph line, בְּי֥וֹם אַפּֽוֹ (oshb:Lam.2.1, byte tier; sweep: 2 verses, byte tier), so the poem's last verse closes an inclusio with its own first verse. The chapter's own PE mark closes web:Lam.2.22.

device_notes: Letters resh, shin and tav close this chapter's acrostic in the same sequence as the standard order, positions unaffected by the letter-order swap earlier in this chapter. SAMEKH continues from web:Lam.2.19 (the front-seam neighbor) across web:Lam.2.20 and web:Lam.2.21 before the chapter's own PE mark closes web:Lam.2.22 (single-witness, tier-3 weak under the Writings addendum). At the front seam, the imperative שִׁפְכִ֤י כַמַּ֨יִם֙ לִבֵּ֔ךְ נֹ֖כַח פְּנֵ֣י אֲדֹנָ֑י (oshb:Lam.2.19, byte tier; "pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord"; this verse also carries a ketiv/qere note per the inventory, not engaged here) stands one verse ahead of this span's own opening prayer, and the same title, אֲדֹנָ֖י (oshb:Lam.2.20, byte tier), stands again inside its report of the sanctuary, so the divine title straddles the seam on both sides. The 1cs speaker and 2ms addressee carried across this span are equally available to the poem's own narrator, whose 1cs already stands at web:Lam.2.11 with 1cs verbs addressing the city at web:Lam.2.13, so the forms alone do not separate the personified city's voice from the narrator's.
